name: Greenbrier Companies

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Builds freight railcars in North America (Mexico-heavy), Europe and Brazil (60% of Greenbrier-Maxion), maintains/refits cars, and rents out an owned fleet of 20,900 railcars. Two plain sentences; model is clear but half cyclical build, half rental.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: FY26 revenue $2,461M (-24%): railcar sales $1,908M (78%), maintenance $358M (15%), leasing and fleet management $195M (8%). Leasing earned $139M of operating profit vs manufacturing $121M.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Railroads, lessors, shippers. One customer was ~12% of FY26 revenue (13% of manufacturing); two were 14% and 12% in FY25. Backlog units 14,000 worth $2.1B, 9% Brazil.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: ~10,000 employees, about half in Mexico; ~5,000 union members, mainly Mexico and Europe. Plants in US, Mexico, Poland, Romania, Brazil (60% JV). Euro/zloty/peso hedged only in part. Revenue-by-country split not extracted; no figure given here.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Sell cars to others or build them for its own lease fleet. Recurring revenue (leasing ex-syndication) is small: leasing segment revenue $195M, 8% of total; fleet grew 22.9% to 20,900 cars at 98% utilization. Margins on manufacturing 9.2% gross in Q4.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Operating margin 5.8% FY26 (143.6/2,461) and 4.3% in Q4 on 31.9% fewer deliveries: high operating leverage. CFO only $39.6M in FY26 (inventories +$107M, cars held for syndication +$97M). FY27 guide 7.0-7.5% margin on $2.8-3.2B revenue; guidance hit rate not assessed.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Inputs: steel, couplers, wheels, axles, brakes; top 10 suppliers are 44% of purchases, top one 14%; customers often specify component suppliers. April 2026 Section 232 expansion to tank cars and components 'materially' raised US tank-car prices; CBP ruled (May, affirmed Sept 2026) Greenbrier evaded AD/CVD on couplers, loss range $0-110M; competitor AD/CVD petition on Mexican tank cars filed Sep 30, 2026. Pass-through works in part via escalators but tariff uncertainty delayed tank-car orders. Signal tags: steel, tariffs, railcar cost, rates, dollar. Single point of failure: Mexico plants and USMCA.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: One of the two largest North American railcar builders; vertical integration (wheels, parts, Mexican component insourcing), integrated lease-and-build with a 20,900-car fleet and syndication. No sign of switching-cost moat in manufacturing; differently now: pushing recurring leasing and programmatic restoration (~2,200 cars).

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: B2B railcar maker; no consumer awareness. Customers are a few dozen large buyers; marketing spend not disclosed.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Rivals: Trinity (the other top-two builder), FreightCar America, specialty builders; Greenbrier says it kept strong share in a down year. Backlog fell 16,600 to 14,000 units y/y (first sequential rise since FY24); Q4 orders 3,400 units vs 3,600 deliveries.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: FY27 guide: industry deliveries 26,000-28,000, revenue $2.8-3.2B, EPS $2.75-3.75 vs $2.60 core FY26. Management says inquiries rose with rail traffic and diesel prices. Lease fleet capex $225-275M net. Runway tied to the build cycle turning; no multi-year target set at an investor day was found.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: FY26 CFO $39.6M, capex $279M, asset sales $193M: net FCF -$47M (FY25 +$63M; FY24 +$6M). Debt $1,837M (recourse $772M, non-recourse $1,066M) vs cash $235M. Returned $56M (div $42.6M + buyback $13.4M). Insiders 2.35%. Pay: EBITDA 40%, ROIC 30%, relative TSR 30%. CEO Tekorius retires Jan 6, 2027. ROIC vs cost of capital not computed from filings; likely below 10% target at trough.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Railcars stay needed; cycle swings are large (FY26 earnings -61%, revenue -24%). Disruption risk low, policy risk high: Mexican output exposed to tariffs, AD/CVD and USMCA. Leasing adds floor. Key-person risk: CEO transition plus new Atlas-nominated director via cooperation agreement.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 4.01/4.02, no NT filings, KPMG clean opinion and effective internal controls, one critical audit matter (purchase invoices). But CBP evasion finding on couplers with up to $110M exposure (not accrued: range 0 to 110), a Superfund liability, non-GAAP adjustments small ($4M). 2024 SEC comment letter (CORRESP Feb/Mar 2024) on the FY23 10-K: outcome file not reviewed.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Boom +, overheat 0 (orders strengthen on rail traffic, but steel/tariff and rates squeeze), stagflation - (costs up, orders delayed), slowdown - (orders weaken, lessor financing costlier). Rate sensitivity: ~$1.1B non-recourse debt, swapped to fixed nearly 100%. Dollar: euro/zloty and peso exposure. Input costs: steel and tariffs.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Pending: CBP coupler AD/CVD case at Court of International Trade (appealed Oct 2026); Commerce/ITC AD/CVD petition on Mexican tank cars (Sep 30, 2026); Section 232 on tank cars and components (April 2026); USMCA review uncertain. Portland Harbor Superfund PRP (cost share undetermined).

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: $38.20 (down from 52w high $59.19), market cap $1.19B, EV ~$2.94B incl. $1.84B debt. Reverse DCF at 10%, 3% terminal: on a normalized owner FCF of ~$140M (my estimate: core net income 83 + after-tax interest ~57 + D&A 130 - maintenance capex assumed equal to D&A) price needs ~8% a year growth for 10 years; on $100M it needs ~12%. Reported FCF is negative so no clean own-history growth rate. P/E 14.7x FY26 core, 11.8x FY27 guide midpoint ($3.25); EV/core EBITDA 9.8x; P/B 0.75x. Own 5-year multiple range and peer P/E not pulled; GATX flagged at top of its price/book range (6.5B cap, $186).

status_reason: Quality is C (thin 5.8% margin, negative net FCF, tariff/customs legal tail of up to $110M); cheap at 0.75x book but no clear mistake yet.
lead_answer: Leasing shift is real but small: leasing is 8% of revenue yet $139M of operating profit versus $121M from manufacturing, and the fleet grew 22.9% at 98% utilization. The build cycle is more likely bottoming than turning down: backlog rose sequentially for the first time since FY24 (14,000 units, Q4 orders 3,400 vs 3,600 deliveries) and FY27 guidance has revenue +14-30% and margin 7.0-7.5%. A slowdown (the regime markets are pricing) and tariffs/AD-CVD on Mexican output are the risks. Catalysts to watch: fiscal Q1 FY27 results (early Jan 2027), CIT ruling on couplers, Commerce preliminary AD/CVD on Mexican tank cars.

feedback.note: Greenbrier says rail traffic increases and elevated diesel prices have boosted railcar inquiries early in FY27 (confirms rail-demand side of regime; overheat). Tariff uncertainty delayed tank-car orders, a policy not macro delay.
Industry deliveries guided 26,000-28,000 for FY27, up from the below-25,000 Trinity guide for 2026 cited in the industry file; supports cycle bottoming rather than slowdown in orders so far.
